commentary:
Energy is running the show again this morning. Brent tacked on another 1.7% to $104.83 and WTI 1.3% to $93.31 after an Iranian official warned the conflict with the US could expand into the Indian Ocean, and the crude complex is flashing genuine physical tightness: Brent's prompt spread blew out to nearly $5 backwardation, the WTI cash roll hit a record, and the WTI-Brent spread is its widest since May. TTF gas jumped 3.4% in sympathy. That oil impulse is feeding straight into the bond market, where the global sell-off deepened and the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest since 2004 — an inflation-plus-fiscal cocktail, with the Fed's first hike in three years still fresh and markets coming round to the idea it has more work to do.

Jobless claims at their lowest since mid-May only reinforce the case. The transmission is textbook: long-end futures took the brunt (US Long Bond -0.3%, Buxl -0.6%, Bunds and OATs lower) while the short end held, steepening the curve; equity indices sagged under the yield pressure, Nasdaq futures off 0.9% and the S&P -0.5%. The dollar hit a fresh two-month peak, dragging gold to $4,301 and silver down 1.3% — real yields and the greenback trumping the geopolitical bid for now. One offset: the Trump-Xi summit opened with the trade truce extended to January 10 and first US-China AI talks confirmed, lifting the KOSPI 1.4%.

Watch the summit headlines, Iran escalation risk, and whether the long end finds a floor — that's the axis for everything else today.
